level_description: Dead-End Stress Test (Deliberately adversarial, not representative of typical usage. Two incidental no-backtrack failures showed up in L4_data_center_topology and DEP_flight_multi_leg_itinerary: greedy decoding committed to a leading digit that, combined with an upper bound capping total digit count, made the field's own lower bound unreachable -- and since this engine never backtracks, that is an unrecoverable dead end. This suite deliberately constructs that shape at graded tightness levels to measure failure rate as a function of how much of the field's range is actually reachable, rather than reporting it as a one-off anecdote. Six cases use a fixed literal threshold (isolating tightness as the only variable); one uses a sibling-dependent threshold (matching the original failure's shape for ecological validity). An initial run showed the model's own greedy default for this prompt is always '85', which trivially satisfies the 10/30/50/70/85 thresholds regardless of tightness -- so tightness alone did not explain failure; DED_tightness_92pct was added specifically to exclude that default and isolate whether a fixed bound can still trigger the failure once the model's preferred value is off the table.

DED_tightness_10pct.name: Percentile Score (tightness ~10%)
DED_tightness_10pct.description: Loosest window: value must be in [10, 96], i.e. ~90% of [0,96] is valid. A leading digit of 1-9 almost always has a viable completion.

prompts.system: You are a scoring service generating a validated percentile score. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a percentile score for a candidate's assessment result.

DED_tightness_30pct.name: Percentile Score (tightness ~31%)
DED_tightness_30pct.description: value must be in [30, 96] -- a leading '0','1','2' each foreclose more of the window than in the 10% case.

DED_tightness_50pct.name: Percentile Score (tightness ~52%)
DED_tightness_50pct.description: value must be in [50, 96] -- roughly the same window-start-to-upper-bound ratio (~0.59) as the DEP_flight_multi_leg_itinerary case that already failed.

DED_tightness_70pct.name: Percentile Score (tightness ~73%)
DED_tightness_70pct.description: value must be in [70, 96] -- only leading digits 7-9 (plus a lucky two-digit 70-96 from a lower start) reach the window at all.

DED_tightness_85pct.name: Percentile Score (tightness ~89%)
DED_tightness_85pct.description: value must be in [85, 96] -- the tightest single-field case: only 12 of 97 possible values are valid, and only leading digit 8-9 has any chance.

prompts.system: You are a scoring service generating a validated percentile score. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a percentile score for a candidate's assessment result.

DED_tightness_92pct.name: Percentile Score (tightness ~94%, excludes model default)
DED_tightness_92pct.description: value must be in [92, 96]. Added after an initial run showed this model's greedy default completion for this exact prompt is always '85', which happens to satisfy every one of the 10/30/50/70/85 thresholds and so never actually stresses the mechanism. This threshold deliberately excludes 85 to test whether a FIXED literal bound (not just a sibling-dependent one) can trigger a genuine dead end once it excludes the model's own default guess.

prompts.user: Generate a percentile score for a candidate's assessment result.

DED_sibling_dependent.name: Sibling-Dependent Sequential Slots
DED_sibling_dependent.description: Matches the original failure's actual shape (DEP_flight_multi_leg_itinerary): the lower bound is not a fixed literal but computed from an already-generated sibling field, so the model can't see the threshold coming from the schema text alone. slot_b must be >= slot_a + 55, capped at 96 -- tightness varies with whatever slot_a the model happens to pick.

prompts.system: You are a resource scheduler generating validated sequential time slots. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate two sequential time slots where the second starts well after the first, within the shift's bounds.
